content: HIRA is a protein in humans encoded by the HIRA gene, located on chromosome 21, centromeric to the COMT gene. The precise function of the HIRA protein has not yet been fully elucidated. However, it is hypothesized to play a role in transcriptional regulation as well as chromatin and histone metabolism. Research conducted by Salomé Adam, Sophie E. Polo, and Geneviève Almouzni suggests that HIRA proteins are involved in the reactivation of transcription following UVC-induced DNA damage. The function of the HIRA gene can be effectively studied using siRNA knockdown techniques, which have been independently validated. Clinically, the HIRA gene is considered a primary candidate in certain haploinsufficiency syndromes, such as DiGeorge syndrome. Insufficient production of the HIRA gene product may interfere with normal embryonic development. Model organisms have been employed to investigate the function of HIRA. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Hiratm1a(EUCOMM)Wtsi, was created as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This initiative is a high-throughput mutagenesis project designed to generate and distribute animal models of human diseases to researchers. Male and female mice from this line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening to assess the effects of HIRA deletion. A total of 22 tests were performed on mutant mice, revealing two significant abnormalities. Notably, no homozygous mutant mice survived past the weaning stage. The remaining tests were conducted on heterozygous mutant adult mice, where a reduction in leukocyte cell numbers was observed in male animals. HIRA has been demonstrated to interact with the protein HIST1H2BK.
